create.name: Cambridge Zen Center
create.bio:
Cambridge Zen Center, whose Korean temple name Daegaksa means Temple of Great Awakening, was started in 1973 by students of the Korean Zen Master Seung Sahn and belongs to his Kwan Um School of Zen. After beginning across the river in Allston, it settled on Auburn Street in Cambridge, Massachusetts, where more than thirty residents now live and practise across three houses. Its guiding teachers include Zen Master Bon Yeon (Jane McLaughlin-Dobisz), who has held the role since 1993, Zen Master Bon Shim and Dyan Eagles, one of the centre's founding members.

The temple keeps a monastic-style timetable of bowing, chanting and sitting every morning and evening, open to anyone without booking. Thursday evenings bring an introductory class for newcomers and a Dharma talk with questions for a teacher; Tuesday evenings and Sunday mornings offer long sits with one-to-one kong-an interviews. A two-day silent retreat is held on the second weekend of each month, and there are affinity groups for young people, elders and BIPOC practitioners, a weekly community dinner, and guest stays and residencies for those who want to try Zen community life.

courses.title: Yong Maeng Jong Jin (YMJJ) monthly retreats
courses.description: A two-day silent retreat on the second weekend of each month, with sitting and walking meditation, chanting, formal four-bowl meals and kong-an interviews with the leading teacher. You may sit one day or both, and first-timers get an orientation on the forms.
courses.price: General Public $75; Members, Seniors, Clergy $55; Students, Teachers in Training $45

courses.title: Guest stays and residency
courses.description: Stays of up to two weeks for people curious about Zen community life, and short- or long-term residencies for those who want to join the household, practising each morning and helping to run the evening programme.

free_resources.title: Daily Practice
free_resources.description: Morning and evening bowing, chanting and sitting in the Dharma Room every day, free and without registration, with guidance on the forms and links to the chanting book.

free_resources.title: Newcomers: Introduction to Meditation and Thursday Dharma Talk
free_resources.description: A free Thursday evening class introducing Zen forms and sitting, followed by a talk from a practitioner and questions for a Zen teacher, then tea.
